verdict.rationale: ObsessionDB's own CHKit tool is described as typed commands to describe, validate, test, and deploy schema and pipelines as code that an agent can drive in CI. Because it speaks the native ClickHouse protocol and HTTP interface, any scriptable ClickHouse client also works unchanged. However, the CI claim is a single marketing line with no documentation of CI setup, non-interactive credentials, or exit-code behavior, and the MCP path relies on OAuth with no API keys. Missing for 10: documented CI/pipeline integration for CHKit, headless or non-interactive authentication such as service tokens, an API or CLI for cluster management, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: CHKit gives them typed commands to describe, validate, test, and deploy schema and pipelines as code: infrastructure an agent can drive, in CI, with a diff you can review.
ObsessionDB speaks the native ClickHouse protocol and HTTP interface, so every ClickHouse client and driver connects unchanged.
